# 057 — "Rebase the remaining branches" does not say where, and the obvious place detaches the owner's checkout

**State:** open
**Source:** `inbox/leg-md-rebase-instruction-detaches-the-owners-checkout.md`, dropped by the
supervisor of leg 110 on 2026-09-13 after doing it and catching it. Filed as a task by leg 111's
inbox drain; the drop is deleted.
**Scope:** doc
**Hardware:** none — one sentence in a generated instruction file and possibly one row in a
recovery table.
**Owner:** required — the remedy is in `.claude/leg.md`, which is generated by
`../../embarch-fleet/scripts/install.py` and which no agent may write, and possibly in
`../../embarch-fleet/ops.md` §3, which is owner-reserved for the same reason.

## What

`.claude/leg.md`'s landing section says, correctly:

> Rebase the remaining branches after each merge.

It does not say **in which working tree**, and the same file spends four paragraphs establishing
that a leg works in a detached worktree at `.worktrees/embarch-doc/leg` *precisely so the owner's
checkout never moves* — including the leg 007 incident where two worktrees shared one branch ref
and left a staged inverse of an entire leg in the owner's index.

Landing `core/057`, leg 110 ran, from the suite checkout:

```sh
cd /home/gabriel/Github/embarch/embarch-doc
git rebase origin/main origin/agent/core/057-serve-outposts-own-answer-doc
```

`git rebase <upstream> <branch>` **checks `<branch>` out**, and a remote-tracking ref checks out as
a detached HEAD. So that one command moved **the owner's working checkout** off `main` and onto a
detached HEAD at the rebase result.

## Why it is worth a rule rather than a "be careful"

- **It is the obvious command.** The branch to rebase is a remote-tracking ref (that is where the
  worker pushed it); the repo it belongs to is the suite checkout; `git rebase <upstream> <branch>`
  is the shortest way to express the instruction as written.
- **It fails silently in the direction that matters.** The rebase *succeeds*, and nothing printed
  reads as a warning. A leg going straight on to its next unit would leave the owner a detached
  checkout with no explanation in any log.
- **It defeats a protection the same file argues for at length.** `--detach` and
  `--force`-is-forbidden exist to keep the owner's HEAD still. This walks around both without
  touching either.

Nothing was lost on 2026-09-13: leg 110 restored it immediately with `git checkout main` (back at
`7937e45`, clean, exactly its step-0 state) and redid the rebase as a `git cherry-pick` inside its
leg worktree, which is equivalent for a one-commit branch and stays where a leg belongs.

## Suggested remedy, for the owner to take or discard

One clause in `.claude/leg.md`'s landing section, and possibly a line in
`../../embarch-fleet/ops.md` §3's recovery table:

> **Rebase in your own leg worktree, never in a repo checkout the owner uses.** `git rebase
> <upstream> <remote-branch>` checks the branch out where you run it, so running it in
> `embarch-doc` detaches the owner's HEAD. For a single-commit branch, `git cherry-pick <sha>` in
> the leg worktree does the same job and cannot reach outside it.

Recovery, if a leg ever leaves it that way: `git -C <repo> checkout main`. The branch is unharmed;
only HEAD moved.

## Related

- `tasks/doc/046` — `check-dispatch.py` cannot see a worktree created in the wrong place. Same
  family: the guard rails are on worktree *creation*, and nothing watches what a leg does to a
  checkout afterwards.
- The code-repo half has the same shape and leg 110 did not hit it only because no code branch
  needed a rebase that leg.

## Done when

- [ ] `.claude/leg.md`'s landing section says which working tree a rebase happens in (owner's
      edit, in `../../embarch-fleet/scripts/install.py`'s template, rendered by `deploy.py`).
- [ ] Optionally, `../../embarch-fleet/ops.md` §3's recovery table carries the "HEAD moved, branch
      unharmed" row and its one-command recovery.
- [ ] Gate green (`../../embarch-fleet/protocol.md` §10).
